1	/****************************************************************************
2	 * arch/arm/include/bk7258/irq.h
3	 *
4	 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
5	 *
6	 * Stage A1 IRQ definitions for the Beken BK7258 (Cortex-M33).
7	 *
8	 * The vector table in bk7258_vectors.c has 80 entries:
9	 *
10	 *   [0]      initial MSP                       (offset 0x000)
11	 *   [1]      __start                           (offset 0x004)
12	 *   [2..15]  14 system exception slots         (offset 0x008 .. 0x03c)
13	 *   [16..63] 48 lower external IRQ slots       (offset 0x040 .. 0x0fc)
14	 *   [64..65] BK7236 app magic "BK7236\0\0"     (offset 0x100 .. 0x104)
15	 *   [66..79] 16 upper external IRQ slots       (offset 0x108 .. 0x13c)
16	 *
17	 * NR_IRQS = 80 makes ARMV8M_PERIPHERAL_INTERRUPTS = 64, so the standard
18	 * NuttX vector layout expects exactly slots [16..79] for IRQs.  The two
19	 * app-magic words at [64]/[65] occupy logical IRQ numbers 48 and 49 and
20	 * are runtime-repaired via arm_ramvec_attach after VTOR switches to RAM.
21	 * This is exactly the layout the T5-AI Tier-1 bootloader
22	 * validates (see docs/bk7258-t5ai/probe/probe.c).
23	 *
24	 * A1 enables interrupts; the common ARMv8-M code needs the NVIC priority
25	 * macros below at compile time, so they are defined here.
26	 * This header is reached via <arch/chip/irq.h> which <arch/irq.h> includes
27	 * BEFORE <arch/arm_m/irq.h> (and hence before nuttx/include/arch/arm_m/
28	 * nvicpri.h), so the priority values are visible when nvicpri.h derives
29	 * NVIC_SYSH_{MAXNORMAL,HIGH,DISABLE,SVCALL}_PRIORITY from them.
30	 ****************************************************************************/
31	
32	#ifndef __ARCH_ARM_INCLUDE_BK7258_IRQ_H
33	#define __ARCH_ARM_INCLUDE_BK7258_IRQ_H
34	
35	/****************************************************************************
36	 * Included Files
37	 ****************************************************************************/
38	
39	#include <nuttx/config.h>
40	
41	/****************************************************************************
42	 * Pre-processor Definitions
43	 ****************************************************************************/
44	
45	/* 64 external interrupts -> vector slots [16..79]; magic at [64]/[65].
46	 * Slots [64]/[65] correspond to external IRQ indices 48/49 but are logical
47	 * NuttX IRQs 64/65 (ETHERNET/SCALE0).  They hold boot magic in flash and
48	 * are runtime-repaired to exception_common after VTOR switches to RAM.
49	 */
50	
51	#define BK7258_IRQ_FIRST                16
52	#define BK7258_EXTERNAL_IRQS            64
53	#define NR_IRQS                         (BK7258_IRQ_FIRST + BK7258_EXTERNAL_IRQS)
54	
55	/* Cortex-M system exception vector numbers (offset by 16 from IRQ number).
56	 * Provided here so chip.h / board code can name them; mirror the values in
57	 * nuttx/arch/arm/src/arm_m/nvic.h.
58	 */
59	
60	#define BK7258_IRQ_NMI                  (2)
61	#define BK7258_IRQ_HARDFAULT            (3)
62	#define BK7258_IRQ_SVCALL               (11)
63	#define BK7258_IRQ_PENDSV               (14)
64	#define BK7258_IRQ_SYSTICK              (15)
65	
66	/* UART1 peripheral sits at chip IRQ 15, which maps to NuttX vector slot
67	 * [16 + 15] = [31].  The slot is already wired to exception_common in
68	 * bk7258_vectors.c, so the vector table itself needs no change.
69	 */
70	
71	#define BK7258_IRQ_UART1                (BK7258_IRQ_FIRST + 15) /* logical 31 */
72	
73	/* Anchor IRQ names for the upper external range.  These logical IRQ
74	 * numbers occupy vector slots [64]/[65] which are also the boot-magic
75	 * slots; runtime repair via arm_ramvec_attach restores exception_common
76	 * after VTOR switches to RAM.
77	 */
78	
79	#define BK7258_IRQ_ETHERNET             (BK7258_IRQ_FIRST + 48) /* logical 64 */
80	#define BK7258_IRQ_SCALE0               (BK7258_IRQ_FIRST + 49) /* logical 65 */
81	#define BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX              (BK7258_IRQ_FIRST + 63) /* logical 79 */
82	
83	/* NVIC priority encoding for the Cortex-M33 core.  The core implements
84	 * priority bits [7:5] (3 bits -> 8 priority levels, top 5 bits
85	 * implemented).  Values are identical to every other stock Cortex-M3/4/33
86	 * in NuttX (see nuttx/include/arch/mps/chip.h); the BK7258 does not add
87	 * anything special here.
88	 *
89	 *   MAX     = 0x00  (highest, exception entry uses this)
90	 *   DEFAULT = 0x80  (midpoint, used by up_irq_save/disable via BASEPRI)
91	 *   MIN     = 0xf0  (lowest)
92	 *   STEP    = 0x10  (16 between adjacent levels)
93	 */
94	
95	#define NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_MIN          0xf0
96	#define NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT      0x80
97	#define NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_MAX          0x00
98	#define NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_STEP         0x10
99	
100	/****************************************************************************
101	 * Stage is CPU0-only; reject NuttX SMP.
102	 ****************************************************************************/
103	
104	#ifdef CONFIG_SMP
105	#  error "A1 gate: BK7258 Stage is CPU0-only; CONFIG_SMP must not be set"
106	#endif
107	
108	/****************************************************************************
109	 * Boot-magic structural constants (image byte offsets, not vector indices).
110	 *
111	 * The Tier-1 bootloader validates a 64-bit app magic "BK7236\0\0" at image
112	 * byte offsets 0x100 and 0x104.  These offsets are determined by the
113	 * original 48-external-IRQ layout: (16 system + 48 external) * 4 = 0x100.
114	 * They do NOT change when external IRQs expand from 48 to 64 in A1,
115	 * because the magic always occupies vector slots [64] and [65].
116	 ****************************************************************************/
117	
118	#define BK7258_MAGIC_BOOT0_OFFSET       0x100
119	#define BK7258_MAGIC_BOOT1_OFFSET       0x104
120	#define BK7258_MAGIC_BOOT_SIZE          8
121	
122	#endif /* __ARCH_ARM_INCLUDE_BK7258_IRQ_H */

# BK7258 N7 — CPU1 单核 AP NuttX 启动链

日期：2026-07-26

## 1. 本 Stage 边界

状态：`static-only`

本 Stage 只实现：

- CPU0/CP NuttX 启动、停止和重新启动物理 CPU1；
- 物理 CPU1 运行独立 `CONFIG_SMP=n` 的 AP NuttX 镜像；
- AP 本地逻辑核编号为 0，入口向量符号为 `__vector_core0_table`；
- 共享 SRAM boot-state 与最小 mailbox doorbell；
- `app.bin` / `app1.bin` 双镜像构建和分段烧录布局。

本 Stage 不实现 CPU2、AP SMP、RPTUN/OpenAMP/RPMsg、Wi-Fi、BLE，也不改官方
`nuttx/` 源码。

## 2. 已收口的硬件事实

状态：`static-only`

- CPU1 启动控制寄存器为 `0x44010014`：bit 0 为 reset release，bit 1 为
  power-down，bit 5 为 RXEVT select，bits 8..31 为 boot address offset。
- 启动顺序固定为：`pwr_dw=0` → `rxevt_sel=1` →
  `boot_address_offset=logical_xip_addr >> 8` → `reset=1`。
- `reset=0` 表示 hold/stop；参考 SDK 的 restart 间隔为 6 ms。
- CPU1 执行 AP image 的 `__vector_core0_table`，AP 本地 logical core 0 对应
  SoC physical CPU1。`0x20000000` 是 SDK 软件 core-ID cell，不是独立硬件身份寄存器；
  本实现由 AP startup 写 local ID 0，并在共享诊断中按 AP offset 报 physical ID 1。
- raw mailbox：CPU0→CPU1 使用 MBOX0 (`0x41000000`)，CPU1→CPU0 使用 MBOX1
  (`0x41020000`)；sender 写 params 后置 ready，receiver 读 params 后置 clear。

## 3. 无重叠布局决策

状态：`static-only`

### 3.1 Flash logical/XIP layout

| 区域 | logical offset | CPU-visible address | size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| bootloader | `0x000000` | `0x02000000` | `0x010000` |
| CP `app.bin` | `0x010000` | `0x02010000` | `0x0f0000` |
| LittleFS | `0x100000` | SDK flash offset `0x100000` | `0x100000` |
| AP `app1.bin` | `0x200000` | `0x02200000` | `0x200000` |

CRC-packed physical offset 使用 `physical = logical * 34 / 32`（所有 partition
边界均 32-byte aligned）：CP 为 `0x11000`，LittleFS 为 `0x110000`，AP 为
`0x220000`。正常更新必须用 BKFIL/bk_loader multi-segment 分别写 boot/CP/AP，
不得用 padding 跨过 LittleFS。可选 factory image 会显式标为会擦除数据区。

### 3.2 SRAM layout

| 区域 | address | size |
|---|---:|---:|
| CP RAM | `0x28000000..0x2804ffff` | `0x50000` (320 KiB) |
| AP RAM | `0x28050000..0x2809efff` | `0x4f000` (316 KiB) |
| shared boot-state | `0x2809f000..0x2809ffff` | `0x1000` (4 KiB) |

当前 CP ELF 的 `.data + .bss` 远小于新 CP 边界；最终是否满足实际运行峰值仍需
板端 `meminfo` 回归。共享页不属于任一 image 的 `.data/.bss/heap`。

## 4. 第一版控制协议

状态：`static-only`

- CPU0 初始化共享页，写 generation/STARTING，然后按固定 SYS 顺序 release CPU1。
- AP startup 写 initial MSP/VTOR/local core ID；NuttX init task 在 heap/SysTick 已建立后
  写 AP_READY、诊断字段和 heartbeat，并通过 MBOX1 发送 READY doorbell。
- CPU0 第一版以 polling 读取 raw mailbox ready + 共享 state；暂不引入 RPTUN 或完整
  SDK mailbox channel stack。
- stop：CPU0 写 STOP command 并通过 MBOX0 doorbell 通知；AP 写 STOPPED + MBOX1 ACK
  后 park；CPU0 `reset=0`，等待 6 ms。超时则执行 forced reset hold。
- restart：stop → 6 ms → start，generation 必须递增。

## 5. 验证门禁

* Linker script for the Beken BK7258 (T5-AI, Cortex-M33) Stage A1 image.
 *
 * Memory map (reverse-engineered on board; the app partition size follows
 * the armino SDK partition table for BK7258):
 *
 *   FLASH : 0x02010000 .. 0x020FFFFF  (1 MiB logical/XIP window)
 *           The on-flash primary_cp_app partition is 1360 KiB (see the
 *           armino BK7258 partition CSVs), so a 1 MiB link window sits
 *           comfortably inside it.  (Stage N1 used a 64 KiB placeholder
 *           because the N1 image was tiny; the full NuttX kernel + NSH is
 *           ~70 KiB and would not fit in 64 KiB.)  The Tier-1 bootloader
 *           jumps the app Reset entry here after validating the BK7236
 *           magic.
 *   RAM   : 0x28000000 .. 0x2809FFFF  (640 KiB SRAM)
 *   MSP   : 0x2809FFFC  (top of usable SRAM, also stored in vector slot 0)
input.new_string:
* Linker script for the Beken BK7258 (T5-AI, Cortex-M33) CPU0/CP image.
 *
 * Stage N7 splits flash and SRAM between two independent NuttX images while
 * preserving the board-verified LittleFS partition:
 *
 *   FLASH : 0x02010000 .. 0x020fffff  (CP logical offset 0x10000,
 *                                      0x0f0000 bytes)
 *   RAM   : 0x28000000 .. 0x2804ffff  (320 KiB CP-owned SRAM)
 *   MSP   : 0x2804fffc
 *
 * Logical flash 0x00100000..0x001fffff remains the LittleFS data partition.
 * The AP image starts at logical 0x00200000 / XIP 0x02200000.  AP RAM starts
 * at 0x28050000 and the top 4 KiB page at 0x2809f000 is shared boot-state.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Expand a BK7258 logical app image into 32-byte + CRC16 flash packets."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import struct
from pathlib import Path

PACKET_DATA = 32
PACKET_TOTAL = 34
APP_MAGIC = b"BK7236\0\0"


def crc16(data: bytes) -> int:
    crc = 0xFFFFFFFF
    for byte in data:
        crc ^= byte << 8
        for _ in range(8):
            crc = (crc << 1) ^ 0x8005 if crc & 0x8000 else crc << 1
    return crc & 0xFFFF


def expand(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    output = bytearray()
    for offset in range(0, len(data), PACKET_DATA):
        block = data[offset : offset + PACKET_DATA]
        block = block.ljust(PACKET_DATA, b"\xff")
        output += block
        output += struct.pack(">H", crc16(block))
    return bytes(output)


def parse_int(value: str) -> int:
    return int(value, 0)


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--in", dest="input", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--xip-base", type=parse_int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--max-size", type=parse_int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--require-magic", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    raw = args.input.read_bytes()
    if len(raw) < 8:
        raise SystemExit("image is too small to contain MSP and Reset vectors")
    if len(raw) > args.max_size:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"image size 0x{len(raw):x} exceeds slot 0x{args.max_size:x}"
        )

    msp, reset = struct.unpack_from("<II", raw)
    reset_addr = reset & ~1
    if not (0x28000000 <= msp < 0x280A0000):
        raise SystemExit(f"MSP 0x{msp:08x} is outside BK7258 SRAM")
    if (reset & 1) == 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"Reset vector 0x{reset:08x} is not Thumb")
    if not (args.xip_base <= reset_addr < args.xip_base + len(raw)):
        raise SystemExit(
            f"Reset vector 0x{reset:08x} is outside image XIP range "
            f"0x{args.xip_base:08x}..0x{args.xip_base + len(raw):08x}"
        )
    if args.require_magic and raw[0x100:0x108] != APP_MAGIC:
        raise SystemExit("CP image is missing BK7236 magic at raw offset 0x100")

    encoded = expand(raw)
    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.out.write_bytes(encoded)

    manifest = {
        "input": str(args.input),
        "output": str(args.out),
        "logical_size": len(raw),
        "physical_size": len(encoded),
        "xip_base": args.xip_base,
        "msp": msp,
        "reset": reset,
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest(),
    }
    args.out.with_suffix(args.out.suffix + ".json").write_text(
        json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    print(json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#
# Role-aware BK7258 post-build packaging.
#
#   CP build -> app.bin, app_crc.bin, legacy nuttx_crc.bin/all-app.bin
#   AP build -> app1.bin, app1_crc.bin
#
# The dual-image build script later combines these as sparse BKFIL segments;
# it never pads across the existing LittleFS partition during normal updates.

set -euo pipefail

TOPDIR="${1:-}"
BOARD_DIR="${2:-}"
ROLE="${3:-cp}"

if [ -z "${TOPDIR}" ] || [ -z "${BOARD_DIR}" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "postbuild.sh: ERROR: TOPDIR and BOARD_DIR are required" >&2
    exit 2
fi

case "${ROLE}" in
    cp)
        RAW_NAME="app.bin"
        CRC_NAME="app_crc.bin"
        XIP_BASE="0x02010000"
        MAX_SIZE="0x000f0000"
        MAGIC_ARG="--require-magic"
        PHYSICAL_OFFSET="0x00011000"
        ;;
    ap)
        RAW_NAME="app1.bin"
        CRC_NAME="app1_crc.bin"
        XIP_BASE="0x02200000"
        MAX_SIZE="0x00200000"
        MAGIC_ARG=""
        PHYSICAL_OFFSET="0x00220000"
        ;;
    *)
        printf 'postbuild.sh: ERROR: unknown role %s\n' "${ROLE}" >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
esac

NUTTX_BIN="${TOPDIR}/nuttx.bin"
RAW_BIN="${TOPDIR}/${RAW_NAME}"
CRC_BIN="${TOPDIR}/${CRC_NAME}"
PACKER="${BOARD_DIR}/scripts/bk7258_crc_expand.py"

if [ ! -f "${NUTTX_BIN}" ]; then
    printf 'postbuild.sh: ERROR: %s not found\n' "${NUTTX_BIN}" >&2
    exit 3
fi

if [ ! -f "${PACKER}" ]; then
    printf 'postbuild.sh: ERROR: %s not found\n' "${PACKER}" >&2
    exit 4
fi

cp "${NUTTX_BIN}" "${RAW_BIN}"
python3 "${PACKER}" \
    --in "${RAW_BIN}" \
    --out "${CRC_BIN}" \
    --xip-base "${XIP_BASE}" \
    --max-size "${MAX_SIZE}" \
    ${MAGIC_ARG}

RAW_SIZE=$(stat -c '%s' "${RAW_BIN}")
CRC_SIZE=$(stat -c '%s' "${CRC_BIN}")

printf 'postbuild.sh: role=%s %s=%s bytes %s=%s bytes\n' \
       "${ROLE}" "${RAW_NAME}" "${RAW_SIZE}" "${CRC_NAME}" "${CRC_SIZE}"
printf 'postbuild.sh: %s physical flash segment @ %s length 0x%x\n' \
       "${CRC_NAME}" "${PHYSICAL_OFFSET}" "${CRC_SIZE}"

if [ "${ROLE}" = "cp" ]; then
    BL_CRC_BIN="${BOARD_DIR}/bootloader/bl_crc.bin"
    if [ ! -f "${BL_CRC_BIN}" ]; then
        printf 'postbuild.sh: ERROR: %s not found; rebuild bootloader\n' \
               "${BL_CRC_BIN}" >&2
        exit 5
    fi

    cp "${CRC_BIN}" "${TOPDIR}/nuttx_crc.bin"
    cat "${BL_CRC_BIN}" "${CRC_BIN}" > "${TOPDIR}/all-app.bin"
    printf 'postbuild.sh: legacy CP all-app.bin=%s bytes\n' \
           "$(stat -c '%s' "${TOPDIR}/all-app.bin")"
else
    rm -f "${TOPDIR}/all-app.bin" "${TOPDIR}/nuttx_crc.bin"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate BK7258 CP/AP packed images and emit split/factory artifacts."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

BOOT_PHYSICAL_OFFSET = 0x000000
BOOT_PHYSICAL_SIZE = 0x011000
CP_PHYSICAL_OFFSET = 0x011000
DATA_PHYSICAL_OFFSET = 0x110000
AP_PHYSICAL_OFFSET = 0x220000
AP_PHYSICAL_END = 0x440000


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def segment(name: str, path: Path, offset: int) -> dict[str, object]:
    size = path.stat().st_size
    return {
        "name": name,
        "file": path.name,
        "physical_offset": offset,
        "length": size,
        "physical_end": offset + size,
        "sha256": sha256(path),
        "bkfil": f"{path.name}@0x{offset:x}-0x{size:x}",
    }


def copy(path: Path, output: Path) -> Path:
    destination = output / path.name
    shutil.copy2(path, destination)
    return destination


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--boot", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--cp-raw", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--cp-crc", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--ap-raw", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--ap-crc", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    for path in (args.boot, args.cp_raw, args.cp_crc, args.ap_raw, args.ap_crc):
        if not path.is_file():
            raise SystemExit(f"missing input: {path}")

    if args.boot.stat().st_size != BOOT_PHYSICAL_SIZE:
        raise SystemExit("bl_crc.bin must be exactly 0x11000 bytes")
    if CP_PHYSICAL_OFFSET + args.cp_crc.stat().st_size > DATA_PHYSICAL_OFFSET:
        raise SystemExit("CP image overlaps the LittleFS physical boundary")
    if AP_PHYSICAL_OFFSET + args.ap_crc.stat().st_size > AP_PHYSICAL_END:
        raise SystemExit("AP image exceeds its 2 MiB logical slot")

    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    boot = copy(args.boot, args.output)
    cp_raw = copy(args.cp_raw, args.output)
    cp_crc = copy(args.cp_crc, args.output)
    ap_raw = copy(args.ap_raw, args.output)
    ap_crc = copy(args.ap_crc, args.output)

    segments = [
        segment("bootloader", boot, BOOT_PHYSICAL_OFFSET),
        segment("cp_app", cp_crc, CP_PHYSICAL_OFFSET),
        segment("ap_app", ap_crc, AP_PHYSICAL_OFFSET),
    ]

    factory_size = AP_PHYSICAL_OFFSET + ap_crc.stat().st_size
    factory = bytearray(b"\xff" * factory_size)
    for item, path in zip(segments, (boot, cp_crc, ap_crc), strict=True):
        start = int(item["physical_offset"])
        payload = path.read_bytes()
        factory[start : start + len(payload)] = payload

    factory_path = args.output / "all-app-factory.bin"
    factory_path.write_bytes(factory)

    manifest = {
        "format": 1,
        "logical_layout": {
            "bootloader": [0x000000, 0x010000],
            "cp_app": [0x010000, 0x100000],
            "littlefs": [0x100000, 0x200000],
            "ap_app": [0x200000, 0x400000],
        },
        "physical_boundaries": {
            "cp": CP_PHYSICAL_OFFSET,
            "littlefs": DATA_PHYSICAL_OFFSET,
            "ap": AP_PHYSICAL_OFFSET,
        },
        "segments": segments,
        "raw_images": {
            "cp": {"file": cp_raw.name, "sha256": sha256(cp_raw)},
            "ap": {"file": ap_raw.name, "sha256": sha256(ap_raw)},
        },
        "normal_update": {
            "preserves_littlefs": True,
            "mode": "BKFIL/bk_loader multi-segment offset-length writes",
            "arguments": [item["bkfil"] for item in segments],
        },
        "factory_image": {
            "file": factory_path.name,
            "length": factory_path.stat().st_size,
            "sha256": sha256(factory_path),
            "preserves_littlefs": False,
            "warning": "Factory image contains 0xff padding across LittleFS",
        },
    }
    manifest_path = args.output / "bk7258-dual-image.json"
    manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build CP app.bin and CPU1 AP app1.bin, then restore the CP build tree.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BOARD_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
CONTEST_DIR="$(cd "${BOARD_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
WORKSPACE="$(cd "${CONTEST_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
TOPDIR="${WORKSPACE}/nuttx"
BUILD="${WORKSPACE}/build.sh"
CP_CONFIG="vendor/openvela/boards/contest2026_135_bk7258/configs/nsh"
AP_CONFIG="vendor/openvela/boards/contest2026_135_bk7258/configs/ap"
JOBS="${JOBS:-8}"
OUTPUT="${TOPDIR}/bk7258-dual"
TMPDIR="$(mktemp -d)"

cleanup()
{
    rm -rf "${TMPDIR}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

build_config()
{
    local config="$1"
    "${BUILD}" "${config}" distclean
    "${BUILD}" "${config}" "-j${JOBS}"
}

save_role()
{
    local role="$1"
    local raw="$2"
    local crc="$3"

    cp "${TOPDIR}/${raw}" "${TMPDIR}/${raw}"
    cp "${TOPDIR}/${crc}" "${TMPDIR}/${crc}"
    cp "${TOPDIR}/nuttx" "${TMPDIR}/nuttx-${role}.elf"
    if [ -f "${TOPDIR}/nuttx.map" ]; then
        cp "${TOPDIR}/nuttx.map" "${TMPDIR}/nuttx-${role}.map"
    fi
}

make -C "${BOARD_DIR}/bootloader" clean all

printf '%s\n' "build_dual_image: building CPU0/CP"
build_config "${CP_CONFIG}"
save_role cp app.bin app_crc.bin

printf '%s\n' "build_dual_image: building physical CPU1/AP"
build_config "${AP_CONFIG}"
save_role ap app1.bin app1_crc.bin

printf '%s\n' "build_dual_image: restoring CPU0/CP build tree"
build_config "${CP_CONFIG}"

rm -rf "${OUTPUT}"
mkdir -p "${OUTPUT}"
cp "${TMPDIR}"/nuttx-*.elf "${OUTPUT}/"
for map in "${TMPDIR}"/nuttx-*.map; do
    if [ -f "${map}" ]; then
        cp "${map}" "${OUTPUT}/"
    fi

    --boot "${BOARD_DIR}/bootloader/bl_crc.bin" \
    --cp-raw "${TMPDIR}/app.bin" \
    --cp-crc "${TMPDIR}/app_crc.bin" \
    --ap-raw "${TMPDIR}/app1.bin" \
    --ap-crc "${TMPDIR}/app1_crc.bin" \
    --output "${OUTPUT}"

cp "${OUTPUT}/app.bin" "${TOPDIR}/app.bin"
cp "${OUTPUT}/app_crc.bin" "${TOPDIR}/app_crc.bin"
cp "${OUTPUT}/app1.bin" "${TOPDIR}/app1.bin"
cp "${OUTPUT}/app1_crc.bin" "${TOPDIR}/app1_crc.bin"
cp "${OUTPUT}/bk7258-dual-image.json" "${TOPDIR}/"

printf 'build_dual_image: artifacts: %s\n' "${OUTPUT}"
printf '%s\n' "build_dual_image: normal split updates preserve LittleFS;"

Base directory for this skill: /home/lijian/project/open-vela/.claude/skills/openvela-build

# openvela Build

编译 openvela 固件、修改内核配置、运行模拟器。

## 默认目标

默认编译目标为 goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap（64 位 ARM 模拟器）：

```
CONFIG_PATH=vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
OUTPUT_DIR=cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
```

如果用户指定了其他板级配置路径，替换上述路径即可。

## 命令

### 编译

```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

示例：
```bash
./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

**成功标志**: 输出 `#### build completed successfully`

**编译产物**: `<OUTPUT_DIR>/nuttx`（ELF）、`<OUTPUT_DIR>/vela_ap.bin`

### 修改内核配置（menuconfig）

```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake menuconfig
```

menuconfig 是交互式 TUI 界面，**不能在 AI 终端中直接运行**。提示用户在自己的终端中执行。

修改配置后保存会自动更新 `.config`。如需持久化到 defconfig：
```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake savedefconfig
```

### 运行模拟器

```bash
./emulator.sh <OUTPUT_DIR>
```

示例：
```bash
./emulator.sh cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
```

**成功标志**: 出现 `goldfish-armv8a-ap>` NSH 提示符

### 清理编译

```bash
rm -rf <OUTPUT_DIR>
```

全量清理后重新编译：
```bash
rm -rf cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ && ./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

## 编译流程

1. 用户指定或确认目标配置路径
2. 执行 `./build.sh <path> --cmake -j$(nproc)`
3. 检查输出最后几行是否包含 `build completed successfully`
4. 如果编译失败，分析错误日志并尝试修复（最多 3 轮）

## 编译失败处理

| 错误类型 | 特征 | 处理 |
|----------|------|------|
| 代码错误 | `error:` + 本驱动文件名 | 自动修复代码，重新编译 |
| 配置缺失 | `undefined reference` + CONFIG 相关 | 提示用户 menuconfig 开启 |
| 工具链问题 | `command not found` | 提示用户安装工具链 |
| 缓存问题 | 奇怪的链接错误 | `rm -rf <OUTPUT_DIR>` 后重编 |

## 启用新驱动的 CONFIG

如果需要临时启用某个 CONFIG 进行编译验证：

```bash
# 方法 1: 直接追加到 defconfig（推荐）
echo "CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680=y" >> <CONFIG_PATH>/defconfig

# 方法 2: 用 sed 修改 .config（临时，不持久化）
sed -i 's/# CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680 is not set/CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680=y/' <OUTPUT_DIR>/.config
```

修改后重新编译即可。

## 常用配置路径

| 目标 | 配置路径 |
|------|----------|
| goldfish-arm64 (推荐) | `vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/` |
| goldfish-arm32 | `vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-armeabi-v7a-ap/` |
| 自定义板级 | `vendor/<vendor>/boards/<chip>/<board>/configs/<config>/` |

Base directory for this skill: /home/lijian/project/open-vela/.claude/skills/driver-code-reviewer

# NuttX Driver Code Reviewer

基于 59 Pattern（52 质量 + 7 设计）的驱动代码质量审查，双轮交叉验证 + 量化评分。
**不修改被审查代码**，Critical 问题仅给出修复建议。

完整 Pattern 定义和维度规格见 `references/layer1-code-quality-spec.md`。

## 外部依赖

| 依赖 | 用途 | 缺失时降级方案 |
|------|------|---------------|
| `nuttx-driver-development` skill | 子系统 pattern 参考 | 仅用本 skill 内置规则 |
| `feishu` skill 或 `feishu-mcp` | 飞书报告输出（可选） | 跳过飞书，仅本地报告 |

## 触发格式

```
review <路径>
review <路径>，对比 <分支名>
```

---

## 维度体系

### 质量维度（L1-1 ~ L1-7，参与评分，100 分制）

| 维度 | 分值 | Pattern 数 | 审查内容 |
|------|:----:|:----------:|----------|
| **L1-1 内存安全** | 20 | 8 | 空指针、UAF、double-free、未初始化、堆泄漏 |
| **L1-2 并发安全** | 20 | 7 | 数据竞争、死锁、锁误用、原子性违反 |
| **L1-3 资源管理** | 10 | 7 | fd/sem/timer/work_queue 申请释放配对 |
| **L1-4 错误处理** | 10 | 4 | 返回值检查、错误传播、状态回滚 |
| **L1-5 类型与数值安全** | 10 | 5 | 整数溢出、符号混用、截断、移位 |
| **L1-6 输入与边界校验** | 15 | 12 | 缓冲区边界、ioctl 参数、格式串注入 |
| **L1-7 嵌入式专项** | 15 | 9 | DMA/cache、ISR、RPMSG、W1C 寄存器、PM |

权重分层依据：
- T0 致命（40%）：L1-1 + L1-2 — 直接导致 crash/数据损坏
- T1 严重（30%）：L1-6 + L1-7 — 攻击入口 + RTOS 独有陷阱
- T2 重要（30%）：L1-3 + L1-4 + L1-5 — 长期影响但很少立即致命

### 维度适用性判定

如果驱动不涉及某维度的检查场景，该维度标记为 **N/A**，其分值按比例重分配到其余适用维度。

| 场景 | N/A 维度 | 理由 |
|------|----------|------|
| 纯 I2C 线程驱动，无 ISR/中断 | L1-7 中 P-47/P-49 跳过 | 无中断上下文 |
| 无 DMA/RPMSG/PM 关键词 | L1-7 整体 N/A | 嵌入式专项不适用 |
| 无并发访问（单线程 chardev） | L1-2 中 P-09~P-14 部分跳过 | 无共享状态 |
| 无外部输入（纯硬件寄存器驱动） | L1-6 部分 N/A | 无用户空间输入 |

**权重重分配公式**：N/A 维度的分值按剩余维度原始权重比例分配。例如 L1-7(15分) N/A 时，15 分按 20:20:10:10:10:15 比例分配到 L1-1~L1-6。

### 独立信号（不参与质量评分）

| 维度 | 扣分上限 | Pattern 数 | 审查内容 |
|------|:--------:|:----------:|----------|
| **L1-8 设计哲学** | -10 | 7 | 抽象层绕过、命名空间污染、影子状态、重复造轮子 |
| **需求/设计一致性** | 独立报告 | — | 对照 requirement.md/design.md 检查功能完整性 |

---

## 评分规则

### 严重度与扣分（L1-1 ~ L1-7）

| 严重度 | 扣分 | 定义 |
|--------|:----:|------|
| Critical | -15 | 导致 crash、数据损坏或安全漏洞 |
| High | -8 | 显著影响代码质量，但不一定立即致命 |
| Medium | -3 | 值得修改但不阻塞 |
| Low | -1 | 改进建议 |

### L1-8 设计哲学扣分（独立）

| 严重度 | 扣分 | 适用 Pattern |
|--------|:----:|-------------|
| High | -4 | DP-01 绕过抽象层, DP-02 跨层依赖, DP-05 板级侵入, DP-06 影子状态 |
| Medium | -2 | DP-03 头文件泄漏, DP-04 缺少 static, DP-07 重复造轮子 |

### 置信度体系

| Pattern Confidence | 评分置信度 | 处理方式 |
|:------------------:|:---------:|----------|
| HIGH | 0.8 | 直接扣分 |
| MEDIUM | 0.6 | 扣分 + 标注需人工确认 |
| LOW | 0.4 | 仅 WARNING，不扣分 |

### 计算

```
维度得分 = 满分(含重分配) - Σ(每个 issue 的扣分)，最低 0 分
总分 = Σ(各适用维度得分)（满分 100）
一票否决：任一维度出现 Critical → 总分封顶 60
```

### 结论判定

| 总分 | 条件 | 结论 |
|------|------|------|
| ≥ 80 | 且无 Critical | **PASS** |
| 60-79 | 或有可修复 Critical | **NEEDS_FIX** |
| < 60 | — | **REJECT** |

### 设计健康度（L1-8，独立输出）

```
设计健康度 = 10 - Σ(DP-pattern 扣分)，最低 0
等级：A(8-10) / B(5-7) / C(0-4)
不影响质量总分和结论判定
```

---

## 执行流程

### Step 0: 收集元信息

从本地收集审查目标的元信息（文件列表、对比分支）。
**主流程不获取文件内容** — 文件内容由每个审查 agent 自行获取，保证独立性。


#### 文件获取策略

1. `get_change` 获取元信息（status, project, branch, patchset）— 401/403 中断并提示检查凭证
2. `get_files` 获取变更文件列表
3. 根据 change status 选择获取方式：

| Status | 获取方式 | branch 参数 |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| **MERGED** | `get_file_content(branch=<target_branch>)` | 目标分支名（如 `trunk`） |
| **NEW/DRAFT** | `get_file_content(branch="refs/changes/XX/<change>/<patchset>")` | XX = change 号末两位，patchset 从 get_files 返回 |

4. **Fallback 链**（任一步骤失败时依次尝试）：
   - `get_file_content` 失败 → `get_diff` 提取新文件内容
   - `get_diff` 失败 → `get_file_lines` 分段读取（每段 500 行）
   - 全部失败 → 跳过该文件，在报告中标注"未获取"

5. .md 文件与 .c/.h 文件同等处理

#### API 限流策略

- 按文件列表顺序逐个读取
- 每个请求间隔 2 秒
- 遇到 409/429：等待 5 秒后重试，最多 3 次
- **获取优先级**：.c/.h 源码文件优先，.md 文档最后获取（丢失可降级，不阻塞审查）

#### 本地路径输入

按优先级检测 diff 范围：
1. 用户显式指定基准：`review <路径>，对比 <分支名>`
2. 未提交改动：`git -C <路径> diff`
3. 已暂存改动：`git -C <路径> diff --cached`
4. 最近 commit：`git -C <路径> diff HEAD~1`

**diff 大小保护**：总变更超过 5000 行时提示用户缩小范围。

### Step 1: 预处理

1. 提取修改文件列表和关键词
2. **维度适用性判定**：扫描代码关键词，标记 N/A 维度并重分配权重
3. **L1-7 动态激活判定**（详见 spec §10.2）：

| 代码区域 | 激活关键词 | 激活的 Pattern |
|----------|-----------|---------------|
| DMA | `dma_`, `DMA`, `up_clean_dcache`, `up_invalidate_dcache` | P-44, P-45 |
| RPMSG/跨核 | `rpmsg_`, `RPMSG`, `shared_mem`, `openamp` | P-46, P-50, P-52 |
| ISR/中断 | `irq_attach`, `_isr`, `_interrupt`, `enter_critical` | P-47, P-49 |
| 硬件寄存器 | `getreg32`, `putreg32`, `modifyreg32`, `REG_` | P-48 |
| 电源管理 | `pm_stay`, `pm_relax`, `pm_resume`, `pm_notify` | P-51 |
| 无匹配 | — | L1-7 标记 N/A，权重重分配 |

4. 识别驱动子系统（sensor/can/fb/lcd/usb/input/charger/其他）

### Step 2: 加载审查规则

1. **Pattern 规格**：`references/layer1-code-quality-spec.md`（59 Pattern 完整定义）
2. **驱动通用规则**：`.claude/skills/nuttx-driver-development/references/coding_rules.md`
3. **子系统规则**（按需）：`.claude/skills/nuttx-driver-development/references/<subsystem>_pattern.md`
4. **设计文档**（如果存在）：搜索变更文件中或同目录下的 requirement.md / design.md

### Step 3+4: 双轮审查

**Round 1**：按 `agents/code-review/prompt.md` 执行 — 52 Pattern 逐项检查（L1-1~L1-7）+ 7 DP-Pattern（L1-8）+ 需求一致性。
**Round 2**：按 `agents/deep-review/prompt.md` 执行 — 侧重内存安全、并发竞态、资源生命周期的深层逻辑分析。

#### 执行模式

**默认模式（并行 subagent，各自获取源码）**：

每个 subagent 在独立上下文中自行读取源码文件并审查。主流程只传递文件路径列表。

```
主流程 Step 0 收集元信息
    ├── Round 1 subagent: 读取源码 → 7 维 Pattern 审查 → 输出 A
    ├── Round 1 subagent: 读取源码 → 7 维 Pattern 审查 → 输出 A
                                                                    （并行执行）
主流程收集 A + B → Step 5 裁判评分
```

**优势**：
- 两个 subagent 完全独立（各自全新上下文，互不可见）
- 不消耗主流程 context 传递大文件
- 两个 subagent 完全独立，互不可见

**Subagent prompt 中必须包含**：
- 变更文件路径列表
- project 名称
- branch 或 patchset ref（`refs/changes/XX/<change>/<patchset>`）
- 变更文件路径列表
- 文件获取 fallback 链（get_file_content → get_diff → get_file_lines）

**降级模式（主流程串行）**：

当 subagent 环境不可用时，在主流程中串行执行：

1. 主流程自行获取所有源码文件
2. 执行 Round 1，输出问题列表 A
3. 插入**视角切换提示**：

```
--- 视角切换 ---
以下进入 Round 2 独立安全审查。
忽略上方 Round 1 的所有结论和问题列表。
以全新的安全审查视角重新审视源码，仅关注：
内存安全深层逻辑、并发竞态时序、资源生命周期对称性、边界条件、错误传播链。
不要重复 Round 1 已报告的表面问题，专注于跨函数/跨状态的深层逻辑。
---
```

4. 执行 Round 2，输出问题列表 B

**关键约束**：无论哪种模式，Round 2 不得基于 Round 1 的结论做判断。

### Step 5: 裁判 + 评分

按 `agents/judge/prompt.md` 在主流程中直接执行：
1. 交叉验证 Round 1 和 Round 2，标注置信度
2. 按 L1-1~L1-7 评分（考虑 N/A 维度权重重分配）+ L1-8 独立信号 + 需求一致性独立报告
3. 生成结构化报告

### Step 6: 输出报告

**默认**：在对话中输出完整结构化报告。

**可选（需用户确认）**：创建飞书云文档。
- 仅在用户明确要求时执行，创建前提示确认
- 如果 `feishu` skill 不可用，跳过并告知用户

1. Primary Request and Intent:

   The user requested the next BK7258 stage: boot a team-owned AP NuttX image on physical CPU1 from the existing CPU0/CP NuttX system.

   Required scope:

   - CPU0/CP NuttX boots physical CPU1.
   - CPU1 runs a separate single-core NuttX image with `CONFIG_SMP=n`.

   - AP vector anchor is `__vector_core0_table`.

     - CP image: `app.bin`
     - AP image: `app1.bin`

   - CPU0 launch sequence must implement the equivalent of:

     ```c
     sys_drv_set_cpu1_pwr_dw(0);
     sys_drv_set_cpu1_rxevt_sel(1);
     sys_drv_set_cpu1_boot_address_offset(ap_base >> 8);
     sys_drv_set_cpu1_reset(1);
     ```

   - AP returns `AP_READY` using shared SRAM boot state plus a mailbox doorbell.
   - Validate later on hardware:
     - physical CPU ID = 1
     - VTOR
     - MSP
     - clock
     - SysTick
     - heap
     - no CP/AP RAM overlap
     - CPU0 NSH/Flash/GPIO regression
     - repeatable start/stop/restart

   - No physical CPU2.
   - No AP SMP.
   - No RPTUN/OpenAMP/RPMsg.
   - No Wi-Fi.
   - No BLE.
   - No unrelated refactoring.

2. Key Technical Concepts:

   - BK7258 tri-core Cortex-M33 role model:
     - physical CPU0 = CP NuttX
     - physical CPU1 = AP logical core 0
     - physical CPU2 is deferred
   - Independent CP and AP NuttX kernels rather than one three-core SMP instance.
   - ARMv8-M Secure-state startup.
   - AP entry through `__vector_core0_table`.
   - NuttX runtime RAM vectors.
   - CRC-packed BK flash format:
     - 32 bytes payload
     - 2 bytes CRC
     - aligned physical mapping:

       ```text
       physical = logical * 34 / 32
       ```

   - Exact CPU1 control register semantics:
     - CPU1 control register: `0x44010014`
     - bit 0: reset release/hold
     - bit 1: power-down
     - bit 5: RXEVT select
     - bits 8..31: boot address field
   - Exact startup polarity:
     - `pwr_dw(0)` = power up
     - `reset(1)` = release/start
     - `reset(0)` = hold/stop
   - Restart reference sequence:
     - stop
     - wait 6 ms
     - start
   - Beken software core-ID cell:
     - address `0x20000000`
     - AP local ID 0
     - SoC physical role derived as local + 1
     - This is a software convention, not an independent hardware identity register.
   - Raw mailbox blocks:
     - MBOX0 `0x41000000`: CPU0 → CPU1
     - MBOX1 `0x41020000`: CPU1 → CPU0
   - First-stage mailbox protocol uses polling rather than the full SDK logical-channel/IRQ stack.
   - Normal firmware updates use sparse/multi-segment BKFIL writes so the LittleFS range is not padded over.
   - A separate factory image is generated and explicitly marked destructive to LittleFS contents.
   - AP image intentionally links no CP SDK peripheral libraries.
   - AP uses only NuttX/NVIC/SysTick/heap/shared-state/raw-mailbox functionality at this stage.

2	"""Pack a minimal BK7236 bootloader into Beken 32-byte-data + 2-byte-CRC flash format."""
3	
4	from __future__ import annotations
5	
6	import argparse
7	import json
8	import struct
9	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
10	from pathlib import Path
11	
12	MAGIC = b'BK7236\x10\x00'
13	MAGIC_LOGICAL_OFFSET = 0x100
14	FLASH_BASE = 0x02000000
15	BOOTLOADER_LOGICAL_SIZE = 0x10000
16	CRC_PACKET = 32
17	CRC_TOTAL = 34
18	BOOTLOADER_PHYSICAL_SIZE = (BOOTLOADER_LOGICAL_SIZE // CRC_PACKET) * CRC_TOTAL
19	DEFAULT_IN = Path('/home/lijian/project/TuyaOpen/zephyr-bk7258-port/out/custom_bootloader/bk7236_min_bl.bin')
20	DEFAULT_OUT = Path('/home/lijian/project/TuyaOpen/zephyr-bk7258-port/out/custom_bootloader/bk7236_min_bl_crc.bin')
21	
22	
23	@dataclass
24	class BootloaderInfo:
25	    input_size: int
26	    logical_size: int
27	    physical_size: int
28	    link_address: int
29	    sp: int
30	    reset: int
31	    magic_logical_offset: int
32	    magic_physical_offset: int
33	    magic: str
34	
35	
36	def crc16(data: bytes) -> int:
37	    crc = 0xFFFFFFFF
38	    for byte in data:
39	        crc ^= byte << 8
40	        for _ in range(8):
41	            if crc & 0x8000:
42	                crc = (crc << 1) ^ 0x8005
43	            else:
44	                crc <<= 1
45	    return crc & 0xFFFF
46	
47	
48	def crc_expand(data: bytes) -> bytes:
49	    out = bytearray()
50	    for off in range(0, len(data), CRC_PACKET):
51	        block = data[off:off + CRC_PACKET]
52	        if len(block) < CRC_PACKET:
53	            block += b'\xff' * (CRC_PACKET - len(block))
54	        out += block
55	        out += struct.pack('>H', crc16(block))
56	    return bytes(out)
57	
58	
59	def physical_offset_for_logical(logical_offset: int) -> int:
60	    return (logical_offset // CRC_PACKET) * CRC_TOTAL + (logical_offset % CRC_PACKET)
61	
62	
63	def prepare_bootloader(data: bytearray) -> tuple[int, int]:
64	    min_size = MAGIC_LOGICAL_OFFSET + len(MAGIC)
65	    if len(data) < min_size:
66	        data.extend(b'\xff' * (min_size - len(data)))
67	
68	    sp, reset = struct.unpack_from('<II', data, 0)
69	    if not (0x28000000 <= sp <= 0x280A0000):
70	        raise ValueError(f'initial SP 0x{sp:08x} outside expected SRAM')
71	    if (reset & 1) == 0:
72	        raise ValueError(f'reset vector 0x{reset:08x} is not a Thumb address')
73	    if not (FLASH_BASE <= (reset & ~1) < FLASH_BASE + len(data)):
74	        raise ValueError(
75	            f'reset 0x{reset:08x} does not target 0x{FLASH_BASE:08x}..'
76	            f'0x{FLASH_BASE + len(data):08x}; rebuild bootloader for 0x{FLASH_BASE:08x}'
77	        )
78	
79	    data[MAGIC_LOGICAL_OFFSET:MAGIC_LOGICAL_OFFSET + len(MAGIC)] = MAGIC
80	
81	    if len(data) > BOOTLOADER_LOGICAL_SIZE:
82	        raise ValueError(f'bootloader 0x{len(data):x} exceeds logical slot 0x{BOOTLOADER_LOGICAL_SIZE:x}')
83	    data.extend(b'\xff' * (BOOTLOADER_LOGICAL_SIZE - len(data)))
84	    return sp, reset
85	
86	
87	def build_image(args: argparse.Namespace) -> BootloaderInfo:
88	    raw = bytearray(args.input.read_bytes())
89	    input_size = len(raw)
90	    sp, reset = prepare_bootloader(raw)
91	    encoded = crc_expand(raw)
92	    if len(encoded) != BOOTLOADER_PHYSICAL_SIZE:
93	        raise ValueError(f'encoded size 0x{len(encoded):x} != expected 0x{BOOTLOADER_PHYSICAL_SIZE:x}')
94	
95	    magic_physical_offset = physical_offset_for_logical(MAGIC_LOGICAL_OFFSET)
96	    if encoded[magic_physical_offset:magic_physical_offset + len(MAGIC)] != MAGIC:
97	        raise ValueError(f'physical magic verify failed at 0x{magic_physical_offset:x}')
98	
99	    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
100	    args.out.write_bytes(encoded)
101	
102	    info = BootloaderInfo(
103	        input_size=input_size,
104	        logical_size=len(raw),
105	        physical_size=len(encoded),
106	        link_address=FLASH_BASE,
107	        sp=sp,
108	        reset=reset,
109	        magic_logical_offset=MAGIC_LOGICAL_OFFSET,
110	        magic_physical_offset=magic_physical_offset,
111	        magic=MAGIC.hex(),
112	    )
113	    args.out.with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(asdict(info), indent=2) + '\n')
114	    return info
115	
116	
117	def existing_path(value: str) -> Path:
118	    path = Path(value).expanduser().resolve()
119	    if not path.exists():
120	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f'path does not exist: {path}')
121	    return path
122	
123	
124	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
125	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
126	    parser.add_argument('--in', dest='input', type=existing_path, default=DEFAULT_IN)
127	    parser.add_argument('--out', type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT)
128	    return parser.parse_args()
129	
130	
131	def main() -> None:
132	    args = parse_args()
133	    args.out = args.out.expanduser().resolve()
134	    info = build_image(args)
135	    print('Minimal BK7236 bootloader image generated:')
136	    for key, value in asdict(info).items():
137	        if isinstance(value, int):
138	            print(f'  {key}: 0x{value:x}')
139	        else:
140	            print(f'  {key}: {value}')
141	    print(f'  output: {args.out}')
142	
143	
144	if __name__ == '__main__':

1	# BK7258 Tier-1 Bootloader (asm trampoline + C main + asm hardened epilogue)
2	
3	This is the Tier-1 rewrite of the hand-written minimal BK7258 bootloader. It
4	keeps the **verified** cold-boot init sequence and jump target (app
5	@ logical `0x02010000`) unchanged, but restructures the binary into three
6	clean layers and adds three Tier-1 features:
7	
8	| Feature | What | Where |
9	|---|---|---|
10	| **I** UART1 boot logging | progress + diagnostics | `boot_main.c` |
11	| **A** FAL partition table parse | locate `app`, derive logical addr | `boot_main.c` |
12	| **J** Hardened jump epilogue | VTOR / dsb / isb / MSP / clear r0-r12 / bx | `start.S` |
13	
14	## Files
15	
16	```
17	board/bk7258_t5ai/bootloader/
18	  start.S                            asm: vectors + bl magic + Reset init + bl c_main + hardened jump
19	  boot_main.c                        C main: FAL parse + app header check + UART logs
20	  bootloader.ld                      FLASH @ 0x02000000, slot 0x10000
21	  Makefile                           arm-none-eabi-gcc freestanding
22	  bk7236_pack_min_bootloader.py      BK CRC packer (copied from $ZEPHYR_PORT/tools/)
23	  README.md                          this file
24	```
25	
26	## Logical / physical layout
27	
28	```
29	FLASH logical base 0x02000000, logical slot 0x10000 (64 KiB)
30	  0x000..0x0FF  vector table  (64 entries: MSP=0x2809F700, Reset, NMI, HardFault, 60x default)
31	  0x100..0x107  bl magic      "BK7236\x10\x00"  (bytes: 42 4B 37 32 33 36 10 00)
32	  0x108..0x1FF  vector table  (62 entries -> Reset_Handler)
33	  0x200..       Reset_Handler : verbatim init -> bl c_main -> hardened epilogue
34	  0x4b8..       .rodata       : FAL partition table (2 entries x 64 B)
35	
36	Physical image (bl_crc.bin): 32 B data + 2 B CRC16 per block -> 0x11000 bytes.
37	Physical slot: 0x0 .. 0x11000 on flash.
38	```
39	
40	### FAL partition table (.rodata, `struct fal_partition`, 64 B/entry)
41	
42	| name | flash_name | offset | len | logical addr |
43	|---|---|---|---|---|
44	| bootloader | beken_onchip_crc | 0x00000 | 0x10000 | 0x02000000 |
45	| app | beken_onchip_crc | 0x10000 | 0x10000 | 0x02010000 |
46	
47	magic_word `0x45503130` (`'E','P','1','0'`), matches the BK SDK
48	`fal_partition.c` / `fal_def.h`. `c_main` scans the table by name, so moving
49	it to a real flash partition later needs no code change here.
50	
51	## Build & pack
52	
53	Requirements: `arm-none-eabi-gcc` (10.3 verified) and `python3`.
54	
55	```bash
56	cd board/bk7258_t5ai/bootloader
57	make            # produces bl.elf, bl.bin (logical), bl_crc.bin (physical)
58	make verify     # nm + .rodata objdump sanity
59	make clean
60	```
61	
62	Build output (verified):
63	```
64	text  data  bss
65	1353     0    0    bl.elf
66	
67	packer:
68	  logical_size: 0x10000      physical_size: 0x11000
69	  sp: 0x2809f700             reset: 0x2000201   (Reset_Handler | 1, Thumb)
70	  magic: 424b373233361000    magic_physical_offset: 0x110
71	```
72	
73	`bss` is 0 on purpose: `c_main` uses only `const` (`.rodata`) and stack
74	locals, so no C-runtime `.bss` zeroing is needed and `start.S` can call
75	`c_main` directly.
76	
77	## Board flashing (bootloader @ physical 0x0)
78	
79	Flash **only** the new bootloader, leaving the existing app probe untouched at
80	logical `0x02010000`:
81	
82	```bash
83	# bl-only flash into the physical bootloader slot [0x0, 0x11000)
84	<tool> --mainBin-multi board/bk7258_t5ai/bootloader/bl_crc.bin@0x0-0x11000
85	
86	# optional bl + app combo (replace <app_crc.bin> with the CRC-packed app image)
87	<tool> --mainBin-multi \
88	    board/bk7258_t5ai/bootloader/bl_crc.bin@0x0-0x11000 \
89	    <app_crc.bin>@0x11000-0x22000
90	```
91	
92	The bootloader physical region is exactly `0x11000` bytes
93	(`(0x10000 / 32) * 34`); flashing outside `[0x0, 0x11000)` is wrong for the bl
94	image. Do **not** run the commands in this repo — build/inspect only; flash on
95	the board with your usual BK tooling.
96	
97	## Expected UART1 log
98	
99	With the existing app probe (which carries its own `BK7236\x10\x00` magic at
100	its `0x100`) flashed at logical `0x02010000`:
101	
102	```
103	u_bootloader enter
104	partition app @ 0x02010000
105	jump to:0x02010000
106	JMP
107	BK7258 PROBE...            <- produced by the app probe after the handoff
108	```
109	
110	If header validation fails, the bootloader prints `BAD` + a short reason
111	(`msp OOR` / `reset no-thumb` / `magic0` / `magic1` / `no app part`) and
112	hangs. UART1 is the same console/GPIO0 TXD + GPIO1 RXD (with GPIO10/11 boot
113	UART state preserved) used by the minimal bootloader.
114	
115	## Rollback
116	
117	If the new bootloader does not start, re-flash the previously verified minimal
118	bootloader image (no C layer):
119	
120	```bash
121	<tool> --mainBin-multi \
122	    /home/lijian/project/TuyaOpen/zephyr-bk7258-port/out/custom_bootloader/bk7236_min_bl_crc.bin@0x0-0x11000
123	```
124	
125	## Design notes / deviations from the spec
126	
127	- **Init sequence is verbatim.** Every register/value in `Reset_Handler` before
128	  `bl c_main` is copied unchanged from the known-good `bk7236_min_bl.S`
129	  (cpsid i, SWD, AON/APB WDT feed, GPIO0/1 + GPIO10/11 UART1 pinmux, UART1
130	  clock + config). Do not edit those constants.
131	- **Jump target unchanged.** Still app @ logical `0x02010000`.
132	- **`flash_cache_disable` skipped.** The BK private cache-control block
133	  (reverse-engineered doc §2.9, base `0xED00E000`, offsets
134	  `0x80`/`0x84`/`0x274`) is not confirmed against the BK7258 register map, and
135	  the verified minimal bootloader never touches cache. Cache disable is an
136	  optimization (avoids stale fetch after VTOR rebase), not a correctness
137	  requirement on a clean cold-boot handoff; the `dsb`/`isb` barriers in the
138	  epilogue already serialize VTOR + MSP writes before the branch. See the
139	  comment block in `start.S`.
140	- **UART TX poll is bounded.** Bit 20 of UART1 status (`0x45830018`) is polled
141	  as "TX-FIFO-not-full" per the spec, but the busy-wait is bounded so that an
142	  inverted bit polarity degrades to the same write-through behavior the
143	  verified minimal bootloader used instead of hanging the boot.
144	- **Hardened epilogue** preserves `r2` (app `Reset_Handler`) while clearing
145	  `r0,r1,r3..r12`, then `bx r2` — mirrors BK §2.7's clear-and-branch.
146

repo — build/inspect only; flash on the board with your usual BK tooling.

83	
84	  /* Decode the runtime core-clock frequency from the live M1/ANA_REG5
85	   * state (read-only) and derive the SysTick reload for one OS tick.  No
86	   * DPLL, mux, voltage or UART-divisor write is performed -- only the
87	   * SysTick reload bookkeeping is recomputed.
88	   *
89	   *   Baseline (M1=0, dplle=0):      cpu_hz = 26000000
90	   *   Loader --reboot 1 (M1=0x423):  cpu_hz = 80000000
91	   *
92	   * systick_initialize() will then arm CLKSOURCE | TICKINT (core clock,
93	   * interrupt on wrap) and attach the SysTick ISR; setting the reload first
94	   * guarantees the first tick has the correct period (some QEMU/model cores
95	   * ignore CTRL writes when RELOAD is zero, so follow the mps_timer.c
96	   * ordering).
97	   */
98	
99	  cpu_hz = bk7258_clockdiag_current_cpu_hz();
100	  reload = (cpu_hz / CLK_TCK) - 1;
101	
102	  putreg32(reload, NVIC_SYSTICK_RELOAD);
103	
104	  /* coreclk=true  -> SysTick clocked at the processor clock (cpu_hz).
105	   * minor=-1      -> do not register a /dev/timerN node; this timer is the
106	   *                  dedicated system clock only.
107	   */
108	
109	  up_timer_set_lowerhalf(systick_initialize(true, cpu_hz, -1));
110	}
111	
112	/****************************************************************************
113	 * Name: bk7258_systick_recalc
114	 *
115	 * Description:
116	 *   Recompute and atomically rewrite the SysTick one-tick reload for the
117	 *   live core clock, after a runtime DVFS frequency switch.  SysTick is
118	 *   clocked at the CPU0 processor clock (CLKSOURCE = processor clock, no
119	 *   /8 divisor), so every CPU frequency change must update RELOAD here or
120	 *   the OS tick period drifts (sleep N becomes N * (old_hz / new_hz)).
121	 *
122	 *   Reads M1/ANA_REG5 via bk7258_clockdiag_current_cpu_hz() (read-only) and
123	 *   writes only RELOAD + CVR.  Clearing CVR after touching RELOAD is the
124	 *   ARMv8-M architecturally mandated sequence to apply a new reload on the
125	 *   next wrap (CVR is write-to-clear).
126	 *
127	 *   This keeps the NuttX common arm_systick.c upstream untouched (the
128	 *   systick_lowerhalf_s.freq field is NOT updated here -- it is only used
129	 *   for usec/count conversions in optional timer APIs, not for the tick
130	 *   cadence, which is governed by RELOAD).  If a future caller needs
131	 *   accurate usec-scale timeouts after a switch, that is a separate task.
132	 *
133	 *   Caller (bk7258_dvfs_set_freq) holds interrupts disabled across the
134	 *   whole mux+reload sequence, so no extra irqsave is taken here.
135	 *
136	 ****************************************************************************/
137	
138	#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_DVFS
139	void bk7258_systick_recalc(void)
140	{
141	  uint32_t cpu_hz;
142	  uint32_t reload;
143	
144	  cpu_hz = bk7258_clockdiag_current_cpu_hz();
145	  reload = (cpu_hz / CLK_TCK) - 1;
146	
147	  /* Use the BK7258_CDIAG_SYSTICK_* address macros (always present in
148	   * bk7258_clockdiag.h) rather than risking a backend-specific
149	   * NVIC_SYSTICK_CURRENT definition.  RVR is RELOAD, CVR is the
150	   * write-to-clear current-counter register. */
151	  putreg32(reload, BK7258_CDIAG_SYSTICK_RVR);
152	
153	  /* Write any value to CVR to clear it; the SysTick then counts down from
154	   * RELOAD so the first tick is one full tick long at the new period. */
155	  putreg32(0, BK7258_CDIAG_SYSTICK_CVR);
156	}
157	#endif /* CONFIG_BK7258_DVFS */

416		---help---
417			Enables support for Symmetric Multi-Processing (SMP) on a multi-CPU
418			platform.
419	
420			N.B. SMP mode requires the use of ARCH_INTERRUPTSTACK:
421	
422			CPU0 thread0  ->  IRQ enter -> add thread0 to block_list -> IRQ leave(crash)
423			                                                        ||
424			                                                        /\
425			                                                       /  \
426			CPU1 thread1  ->  block_task -> take thread0 from block_list -> run thread0
427

429			will caused IRQ handler stack corruption.
430	
431	config BMP
432		bool "Bound Multi-Processing (BMP)"
433		depends on ARCH_HAVE_MULTICPU
434		---help---
435			Enables support for Bound Multi-Processing (BMP) on a multi-CPU
436			platform. Bound multiprocessing provides the scheduling control
437			of an asymmetric multiprocessing model, while preserving the
438			hardware abstraction and management of symmetric multiprocessing.
439	
440			BMP is similar to SMP, but you can specify which processors a thread
441			can run on. You can use both SMP and BMP on the same system, allowing
442			some threads to migrate from one processor to another, while other
443			threads are restricted to one or more processors.
444	
445			As with SMP, a single copy of the OS maintains an overall view of all
446			system resources, allowing them to be dynamically allocated and shared
447			among applications. But, during application initialization, a setting
448			determined by the system designer forces all of an application's threads
449			to execute only on a specified CPU.
450	
451			Compared to full, floating SMP operation, this approach offers several
452			advantages:
453	
454			1. It eliminates the cache thrashing that can reduce performance in an SMP
455			system by allowing applications that share the same data set to run
456			exclusively on the same CPU.
457			2. It offers simpler application debugging than SMP since all execution
458			threads within an application run on a single CPU.
459			3. It helps legacy applications that use poor techniques for synchronizing
460			shared data to run correctly, again by letting them run on a single CPU.
461	
462	endchoice

792	
793	config SCHED_HAVE_PARENT
794		bool "Support parent/child task relationships"
795		default n
796		---help---
797			Remember the ID of the parent task when a new child task is
798			created.  This support enables some additional features (such as
799			SIGCHLD) and modifies the behavior of other interfaces.  For
800			example, it makes waitpid() more standards complete by restricting
801			the waited-for tasks to the children of the caller. Default:
802			disabled.
803	
804	config SCHED_CHILD_STATUS
805		bool "Retain child exit status"
806		default n
807		depends on SCHED_HAVE_PARENT
808		---help---
809			If this option is selected, then the exit status of the child task
810			will be retained after the child task exits.  This option should be
811			selected if you require knowledge of a child process's exit status.
812			Without this setting, wait(), waitpid() or waitid() may fail.  For
813			example, if you do:
814	
815			1) Start child task
816			2) Wait for exit status (using wait(), waitpid(), or waitid()).
817	
818			This can fail because the child task may run to completion before
819			the wait begins.  There is a non-standard work-around in this case:
820			The above sequence will work if you disable pre-emption using
821			sched_lock() prior to starting the child task, then re-enable pre-
822			emption with sched_unlock() after the wait completes.  This works
823			because the child task is not permitted to run until the wait is in
824			place.
825	
826			The standard solution would be to enable SCHED_CHILD_STATUS.  In
827			this case the exit status of the child task is retained after the
828			child exits and the wait will successful obtain the child task's
829			exit status whether it is called before the child task exits or not.
830	
831			Warning:  If you enable this feature, then your application must
832			either (1) take responsibility for reaping the child status with wait(),
833			waitpid(), or waitid(), or (2) suppress retention of child status.
834			If you do not reap the child status, then you have a memory leak and
835			your system will eventually fail.
836	
837			Retention of child status can be suppressed on the parent using logic like:
838	
839				struct sigaction sa;
840	
841				sa.sa_handler = SIG_IGN;
842				sa.sa_flags = SA_NOCLDWAIT;
843				int ret = sigaction(SIGCHLD, &sa, NULL);
844	
845	if SCHED_CHILD_STATUS
846	
847	config PREALLOC_CHILDSTATUS
848		int "Number of pre-allocated child status"
849		default 0
850		---help---
851			To prevent runaway child status allocations and to improve
852			allocation performance, child task exit status structures are pre-
853			allocated when the system boots.  This setting determines the number
854			of child status structures that will be pre-allocated.
855	
856			However, the number of child status structures may need to be
857			significantly larger because this number includes the maximum number
858			of tasks that are running PLUS the number of tasks that have exit'ed
859			without having their exit status reaped (via wait(), waitid(), or
860			waitpid()).
861	
862			Obviously, if tasks spawn children indefinitely and never have the
863			exit status reaped, then you may have a memory leak!  If you enable
864			the SCHED_CHILD_STATUS feature, then your application must take
865			responsibility for either (1) reaping the child status with wait(),
866			waitpid(), or waitid() or it must (2) suppress retention of child
867			status.  Otherwise, your system will eventually fail.
868	
869			Retention of child status can be suppressed on the parent using logic like:
870	
871				struct sigaction sa;
872	
873				sa.sa_handler = SIG_IGN;
874				sa.sa_flags = SA_NOCLDWAIT;
875				int ret = sigaction(SIGCHLD, &sa, NULL);

1139	config SCHED_CPULOAD_SYSCLK

1142			If this option is enabled, the system clock is used for cpu load
1143			measurement by default.
1144	
1145			There is a serious issue for the accuracy of measurements if the
1146			system clock is used, however.  NuttX threads are often started at
1147			the time of the system timer expiration.  Others may be stopped at
1148			the time of the system timer expiration (if round-robin time-slicing
1149			is enabled).  Such thread behavior occurs synchronously with the
1150			system timer and, hence, is not randomly sampled.  As a consequence,
1151			the CPU load attributed to these threads that run synchronously with
1152			they system timer may be grossly in error.
1153			The CPU load measurements are determined by sampling the active
1154			tasks periodically at the occurrence to a timer expiration.
1155			If tickless is enabled, SYSCLK should not be used. Its error will be
1156			very large, and using it for analysis will lead to wrong conclusions.
1157	
1158	config SCHED_CPULOAD_EXTCLK
1159		bool "Use external clock"

1161			There is a serious issue for the accuracy of measurements if the
1162			system clock is used, however.  NuttX threads are often started at

1164			the time of the system timer expiration (if round-robin time-slicing
1165			is enabled).  Such thread behavior occurs synchronously with the
1166			system timer and, hence, is not randomly sampled.  As a consequence,
1167			the CPU load attributed to these threads that run synchronously with
1168			they system timer may be grossly in error.
1169	
1170			The solution is to use some other clock that runs at a different
1171			rate and has timer expirations that are asynchronous with the

1598	config BOARD_EARLY_INITIALIZE
1599		bool "Custom board early initialization"
1600		default n
1601		---help---
1602			There are three points in time where you can insert custom,
1603			board-specific initialization logic:
1604	
1605			1) <arch>_board_initialize():  This function is used only for
1606			initialization of very low-level things like configuration of
1607			GPIO pins, power setting.  The OS has not been initialized
1608			at this point, so you cannot allocate memory or initialize
1609			device drivers at this phase.
1610	
1611			2) The next level of initialization is performed by a call to
1612			up_initialize() (in arch/<arch>/src/common/up_initialize.c).
1613			The OS has been initialized at this point and it is okay to
1614			initialize drivers in this phase.
1615	
1616			At this same point in time, the OS will also call a board-
1617			specific initialization function named board_early_initialize()
1618			if CONFIG_BOARD_EARLY_INITIALIZE is selected.  The context in
1619			which board_early_initialize() executes is suitable for early
1620			initialization of most, simple device drivers and is a logical,
1621			board-specific extension of up_initialize().
1622	
1623			board_early_initialize() runs on the startup, initialization thread.
1624			Some initialization operations cannot be performed on the start-up,
1625			initialization thread.  That is because the initialization thread
1626			cannot wait for event.  Waiting may be required, for example, to
1627			mount a file system or or initialize a device such as an SD card.
1628			For this reason, such driver initialize must be deferred to
1629			board_late_initialize().
1630	
1631			3) And, finally, just before the user application code starts.
1632	
1633			If CONFIG_BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE is selected, then an additional
1634			initialization call will be performed in the boot-up sequence to a
1635			function called board_late_initialize().  board_late_initialize()
1636			will be called after up_initialize() is called and just before the
1637			main application is started.  This additional initialization
1638			phase may be used, for example, to initialize more complex,
1639			board-specific device drivers.
1640	
1641			Waiting for events, use of I2C, SPI, etc are permissible in the
1642			context of board_late_initialize().  That is because
1643			board_late_initialize() will run on a temporary, internal kernel
1644			thread.
1645	
1646	config BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE
1647		bool "Custom board late initialization"
1648		default n
1649		---help---
1650			There are three points in time where you can insert custom,
1651			board-specific initialization logic:
1652	
1653			1) <arch>_board_initialize():  This function is used only for
1654			initialization of very low-level things like configuration of
1655			GPIO pins, power setting.  The OS has not been initialized
1656			at this point, so you cannot allocate memory or initialize
1657			device drivers at this phase.
1658	
1659			2) The next level of initialization is performed by a call to
1660			up_initialize() (in arch/<arch>/src/common/up_initialize.c).
1661			The OS has been initialized at this point and it is okay to
1662			initialize drivers in this phase.
1663	
1664			At this same point in time, the OS will also call a board-
1665			specific initialization function named board_early_initialize()
1666			if CONFIG_BOARD_EARLY_INITIALIZE is selected.  The context in
1667			which board_early_initialize() executes is suitable for early
1668			initialization of most, simple device drivers and is a logical,
1669			board-specific extension of up_initialize().
1670	
1671			board_early_initialize() runs on the startup, initialization thread.
1672			Some initialization operations cannot be performed on the start-up,
1673			initialization thread.  That is because the initialization thread
1674			cannot wait for event.  Waiting may be required, for example, to
1675			mount a file system or or initialize a device such as an SD card.
1676			For this reason, such driver initialize must be deferred to
1677			board_late_initialize().
1678	
1679			3) And, finally, just before the user application code starts.
1680	
1681			If CONFIG_BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE is selected, then an additional
1682			initialization call will be performed in the boot-up sequence to a
1683			function called board_late_initialize().  board_late_initialize()
1684			will be called after up_initialize() is called and just before the
1685			main application is started.  This additional initialization
1686			phase may be used, for example, to initialize more complex,
1687			board-specific device drivers.
1688	
1689			Waiting for events, use of I2C, SPI, etc are permissible in the
1690			context of board_late_initialize().  That is because
1691			board_late_initialize() will run on a temporary, internal kernel
1692			thread.
1693	
1694	if BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE

1697		int "Board initialization thread stack size"
1698		default DEFAULT_TASK_STACKSIZE
1699		---help---
1700			The size of the stack to allocate when starting the board
1701			initialization thread.

1898	config SCHED_WORKQUEUE

1900		default n

1904	
1905	config WQUEUE_NOTIFIER
1906		bool "Generic work notifier"
1907		default n
1908		depends on SCHED_WORKQUEUE
1909		---help---
1910			Enable building of work queue notifier logic that will execute a
1911			worker function an event occurs.  This is is a general purpose
1912			notifier, but was developed specifically to support poll() logic
1913			where the poll must wait for an resources to become available.
1914	
1915	config SCHED_HPWORK
1916		bool "High priority (kernel) worker thread"
1917		default n
1918		select SCHED_WORKQUEUE
1919		---help---
1920			Create a dedicated high-priority "worker" thread to handle delayed
1921			processing from interrupt handlers.  This feature is required for
1922			some drivers but, if there are no complaints, can be safely
1923			disabled.  The high priority worker thread also performs garbage
1924			collection -- completing any delayed memory deallocations from
1925			interrupt handlers.  If the high-priority worker thread is disabled,
1926			then that clean up will be performed either by (1) the low-priority
1927			worker thread, if enabled, and if not (2) the IDLE thread instead
1928			(which runs at the lowest of priority and may not be appropriate if
1929			memory reclamation is of high priority)
1930	
1931			For other, less-critical asynchronous or delayed process, the
1932			low-priority worker thread is recommended.
1933	
1934	if SCHED_HPWORK
1935	
1936	config SCHED_HPNTHREADS
1937		int "Number of high-priority worker threads"
1938		default 1
1939		---help---
1940			This options selects multiple, high-priority threads.  This is
1941			essentially a "thread pool" that provides multi-threaded servicing
1942			of the high-priority work queue.  This breaks the serialization
1943			of the "queue" (hence, it is no longer a queue at all).
1944	
1945			CAUTION: Some drivers may use the work queue to serialize
1946			operations.  They may also use the high-priority work queue if it is
1947			available.  If there are multiple high-priority worker threads, then
1948			this can result in the loss of that serialization.  There may be
1949			concurrent driver operations running on different HP threads and
1950			this could lead to a failure.  You may need to visit the use of the
1951			HP work queue on your configuration is you select
1952			CONFIG_SCHED_HPNTHREADS > 1
1953	
1954	config SCHED_HPWORKPRIORITY
1955		int "High priority worker thread priority"
1956		default 224
1957		---help---
1958			The execution priority of the higher priority worker thread.
1959	
1960			The higher priority worker thread is intended to serve as the
1961			"bottom" half for device drivers.  As a consequence it must run at
1962			a very high, fixed priority.  Typically, it should be the highest
1963			priority thread in your system.  Default: 224
1964	
1965			For lower priority, application oriented worker thread support,
1966			please consider enabling the lower priority work queue.  The lower
1967			priority work queue runs at a lower priority, of course, but has
1968			the added advantage that it supports "priority inheritance" (if
1969			PRIORITY_INHERITANCE is also selected):  The priority of the lower
1970			priority worker thread can then be adjusted to match the highest
1971			priority client.
1972	
1973	config SCHED_HPWORKSTACKSIZE
1974		int "High priority worker thread stack size"
1975		default DEFAULT_TASK_STACKSIZE
1976		---help---
1977			The stack size allocated for the worker thread.  Default: 2K.
1978	
1979	config SCHED_HPWORKSTACKSECTION
1980		string "The section where hpwork stack is located"
1981		default ""
1982		---help---
1983			The section where hpwork stack is located.
1984	
1985	endif # SCHED_HPWORK
1986	
1987	config SCHED_LPWORK
1988		bool "Low priority (kernel) worker thread"
1989		default n
1990		select SCHED_WORKQUEUE
1991		---help---
1992			If SCHED_LPWORK is defined then a lower-priority work queue will
1993			be created.  This lower priority work queue is better suited for
1994			more extended, application oriented processing (such as file system
1995			clean-up operations or asynchronous I/O)

1999	config SCHED_LPNTHREADS
2000		int "Number of low-priority worker threads"
2001		default 1 if !FS_AIO
2002		default 4 if FS_AIO
2003		---help---
2004			This options selects multiple, low-priority threads.  This is
2005			essentially a "thread pool" that provides multi-threaded servicing
2006			of the low-priority work queue.  This breaks the serialization
2007			of the "queue" (hence, it is no longer a queue at all).
2008	
2009			This options is required to support, for example, I/O operations
2010			that stall waiting for input.  If there is only a single thread,
2011			then the entire low-priority queue processing stalls in such cases.
2012			Such behavior is necessary to support asynchronous I/O, AIO (for
2013			example).
2014	
2015			CAUTION: Some drivers may use the work queue to serialize
2016			operations.  They may also use the low-priority work queue if it is
2017			available.  If there are multiple low-priority worker threads, then
2018			this can result in the loss of that serialization.  There may be
2019			concurrent driver operations running on different LP threads and
2020			this could lead to a failure.  You may need to visit the use of the
2021			LP work queue on your configuration is you select
2022			CONFIG_SCHED_LPNTHREADS > 1
2023	
2024	config SCHED_LPWORKPRIORITY
2025		int "Low priority worker thread priority"
2026		default 100

直接回答：

1. **对，当前没有编译或链接 Beken/Armino 的 AP 侧库。**  
   当前 `app1.bin` 编译的是：
   - AP 独立 NuttX 内核及 NuttX 自身库；
   - team-overlay 的 vector、startup、IRQ、SysTick、heap、AP main；
   - 共享 SRAM 和最小 mailbox 实现。

   这是 N7 为了先验证 CPU1 最小启动链而有意做的裁剪，但它只代表“最小 AP NuttX 镜像可构建”，**不代表完整 AP SDK/BSP 已适配**。

2. **不是所有实现都使用了 wrapper 模式。当前是混合模式。**
   - CPU0 控制 CPU1：属于 wrapper，包装了 CP SDK 的四个接口：
     `sys_drv_set_cpu1_pwr_dw()`、`rxevt_sel()`、`boot_address_offset()`、`reset()`。
   - AP SysTick、IRQ、heap：直接使用 NuttX 接口。
   - AP vector、reset startup、linker：team-owned 直接实现，这些启动前代码本身也不能完全依赖普通 wrapper。
   - raw mailbox：目前是直接 MMIO，不是 SDK mailbox wrapper。
   - shared SRAM 状态机：team-owned 直接实现，不是 SDK wrapper。

3. **所以如果你的要求是“AP 侧库也必须编译，并且除必要 startup/linker 外都通过 wrapper 隔离 SDK”，那么当前实现不满足这个要求。**

准确描述当前架构是：

```text
CPU0：CP SDK API wrapper
CPU1：NuttX-native 最小实现 + 部分直接 MMIO

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
3	#
4	# setup_bk7258_sdk.sh -- validate or install the BK7258 T5-AI SDK bundle.
5	#
6	# This script manages the local Beken SDK prebuilt library bundle that lives
7	# under board/bk7258_t5ai/bk_idk/armino_as_lib/cp/.  The bundle is a local
8	# prerequisite and is NOT committed to this repository because it contains
9	# Beken proprietary/restricted prebuilts.
10	#
11	# Usage:
12	#   setup_bk7258_sdk.sh --check  [cp-dir]   Validate bundle structure and checksums
13	#   setup_bk7258_sdk.sh --install <cp-dir>   Install from authorized SDK source
14	#   setup_bk7258_sdk.sh --help               Show this help
15	#
16	# The script performs no network download and no privilege escalation.
17	# The source for --install must be an authorized Beken/Tuya SDK
18	# armino_as_lib/cp bundle obtained separately.
19	
20	set -euo pipefail
21	
22	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
23	# Constants
24	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
25	
26	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
27	BOARD_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
28	MANIFEST="${SCRIPT_DIR}/bk7258_sdk_manifest.sha256"
29	DEFAULT_TARGET="${BOARD_DIR}/bk_idk/armino_as_lib/cp"
30	
31	PROG="$(basename "$0")"
32	
33	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
34	# Helpers
35	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
36	
37	die() {
38	    printf '%s: error: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2
39	    exit 1
40	}
41	
42	info() {
43	    printf '%s: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2
44	}
45	
46	usage() {
47	    cat <<EOF
48	Usage:
49	  $PROG --check  [cp-dir]   Validate bundle structure and checksums
50	  $PROG --install <cp-dir>   Install from authorized SDK source
51	  $PROG --help               Show this help
52	
53	Options:
54	  --check [cp-dir]   Validate that the directory has the expected structure
55	                     (include/, config/, libs/) and that all entries in the
56	                     tracked checksum manifest pass sha256sum -c.
57	                     Defaults to the standard installed location if omitted.
58	
59	  --install <cp-dir> Copy an authorized Beken/Tuya SDK cp bundle into the
60	                     standard installed location.  Refuses if the destination
61	                     already exists.  Uses atomic rename: copies to a temp
62	                     sibling directory, validates checksums, then renames.
63	                     Cleans only its own temp directory on failure.
64	
65	  --help             Show this help message and exit.
66	
67	No network download is performed.  The source must be an authorized
68	Beken/Tuya SDK armino_as_lib/cp bundle obtained separately.
69	EOF
70	}
71	
72	# validate_structure <dir>
73	#   Check that the given directory contains the expected subdirectories.
74	validate_structure() {
75	    local dir="$1"
76	    local ok=true
77	
78	    for subdir in include config libs; do
79	        if [[ ! -d "${dir}/${subdir}" ]]; then
80	            printf '  missing: %s/%s\n' "$dir" "$subdir" >&2
81	            ok=false
82	        fi
83	    done
84	
85	    if [[ "$ok" == "false" ]]; then
86	        return 1
87	    fi
88	    return 0
89	}
90	
91	# validate_manifest <cp-dir>
92	#   Run sha256sum -c against the tracked manifest from the given cp root.
93	#   Fail-closed: any nonzero exit from sha256sum (missing files, read errors,
94	#   or hash mismatches) triggers an immediate failure.  Useful diagnostics are
95	#   preserved on stderr.
96	validate_manifest() {
97	    local cp_dir="$1"
98	
99	    if [[ ! -f "$MANIFEST" ]]; then
100	        die "tracked manifest not found: ${MANIFEST}"
101	    fi
102	
103	    info "validating checksums against ${MANIFEST} ..."
104	    local output
105	    output=$(cd "$cp_dir" && sha256sum -c "$MANIFEST" 2>&1) || {
106	        echo "$output" | grep -v ": OK$" | head -30 >&2
107	        die "checksum validation failed (see diagnostics above)"
108	    }
109	
110	    info "all checksums OK"
111	}
112	
113	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
114	# Argument parsing
115	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
116	
117	MODE=""
118	CP_DIR=""
119	
120	if [[ $# -lt 1 ]]; then
121	    usage >&2
122	    exit 1
123	fi
124	
125	case "$1" in
126	    --check)
127	        MODE="check"
128	        CP_DIR="${2:-${DEFAULT_TARGET}}"
129	        ;;
130	    --install)
131	        MODE="install"
132	        if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
133	            die "--install requires a <cp-dir> argument"
134	        fi
135	        CP_DIR="$2"
136	        ;;
137	    --help|-h)
138	        usage
139	        exit 0
140	        ;;
141	    *)
142	        die "unknown option: $1 (try --help)"
143	        ;;
144	esac
145	
146	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
147	# --check mode
148	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
149	
150	do_check() {
151	    local cp_dir="$1"
152	
153	    info "checking SDK bundle at: ${cp_dir}"
154	
155	    if [[ ! -d "$cp_dir" ]]; then
156	        die "directory does not exist: ${cp_dir}"
157	    fi
158	
159	    info "validating directory structure ..."
160	    if ! validate_structure "$cp_dir"; then
161	        die "directory structure validation failed"
162	    fi
163	    info "directory structure OK"
164	
165	    validate_manifest "$cp_dir"
166	
167	    info "check PASSED"
168	}
169	
170	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
171	# --install mode
172	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
173	
174	do_install() {
175	    local src_dir="$1"
176	    local dst_dir="$DEFAULT_TARGET"
177	    local tmp_dir="${dst_dir}.tmp.$$"
178	
179	    info "source:      ${src_dir}"
180	    info "destination: ${dst_dir}"
181	
182	    # Refuse if destination already exists
183	    if [[ -e "$dst_dir" ]]; then
184	        die "destination already exists: ${dst_dir} -- will not overwrite or delete.  Remove it manually first if you intend to replace it."
185	    fi
186	
187	    # Validate source structure
188	    info "validating source structure ..."
189	    if ! validate_structure "$src_dir"; then
190	        die "source directory structure validation failed"
191	    fi
192	    info "source structure OK"
193	
194	    # Ensure destination parent exists (cp -a needs it for the temp sibling)
195	    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dst_dir")"
196	
197	    # Clean up temp directory if it exists from a previous failed run
198	    if [[ -e "$tmp_dir" ]]; then
199	        info "removing leftover temp directory: ${tmp_dir}"
200	        rm -rf "$tmp_dir"
201	    fi
202	
203	    # Ensure cleanup on failure
204	    cleanup() {
205	        if [[ -e "$tmp_dir" ]]; then
206	            info "cleaning up temp directory: ${tmp_dir}"
207	            rm -rf "$tmp_dir"
208	        fi
209	    }
210	    trap cleanup ERR
211	
212	    # Copy to temp directory
213	    info "copying to temporary directory ..."
214	    cp -a "$src_dir" "$tmp_dir"
215	
216	    # Validate checksums from the temp copy
217	    info "validating checksums on copied bundle ..."
218	    (cd "$tmp_dir" && sha256sum -c "$MANIFEST" --quiet) || {
219	        cleanup
220	        die "checksum validation failed on copied bundle"
221	    }
222	    info "checksums OK on copied bundle"
223	
224	    # Atomic rename
225	    info "renaming into place ..."
226	    mv "$tmp_dir" "$dst_dir"
227	
228	    # Disable cleanup trap (success)
229	    trap - ERR
230	
231	    info "install PASSED -- SDK bundle at: ${dst_dir}"
232	}
233	
234	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
235	# Main
236	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
237	
238	case "$MODE" in
239	    check)
240	        do_check "$CP_DIR"
241	        ;;
242	    install)
243	        do_install "$CP_DIR"
244	        ;;
245	esac
